headline: Approved lot-width variances for the 34-lot Wellington Road subdivision, 4-1; denied a garage at 114 Glen Bloom Drive.
summary: Neighbors opposed the 34-lot Wellington Road subdivision and a garage at 114 Glen Bloom Drive. Several small approvals covered homes on Walnut Street, Aladdin Street, and Hazelton Court. The request for 18 Geneva Street was withdrawn, and 218 South Lincoln Street was moved to a later date.
decisions: Approved variances for a garage at 366 Walnut Street, with a condition that a survey be required, 5-0.
Denied variances for a 32-by-40-foot garage at 114 Glen Bloom Drive, 5-0.
Approved withdrawal of the request for a house at 18 Geneva Street, 5-0.
Moved the request for 218 South Lincoln Street to a later date, with new notices to be mailed.
Approved a variance for a porch at 82 Aladdin Street, 5-0.
Approved keeping a shed about 6 inches from the side lot line at 128 Hazelton Court, 5-0.
Approved driveway and parking variances at 550 River Road, 5-0.
Approved variances for the subdivision of 4 Bremer Street, with conditions on driveways and a 20-foot landscape buffer, 5-0.
Approved six lot-width variances for the Wellington Road subdivision, 4-1.
Denied the rehearing request for the 34-lot Wellington Road subdivision approval, 4-1.
Denied a second rehearing request for the 34-lot Wellington Road subdivision approval, 4-1.
Accepted the June 11, 2026 minutes, as amended, 5-0.

it closer to his property and does not believe it is currently on conservation land. Also, if he builds 100 
the garage, the garden will be removed.  101 
 102 
Acting Vice Chairman Taylor asked how many cars will be worked on and kept at the property at 103 
any given time. Mr. Bryer stated that he currently has a few classic cars and has to pay to have 104 
them stored offsite. He would like to bring these onsite. The cars will be kept in the garage, out 105

Jon Delmar, 111 Glen Bloom Drive, stated that he does not believe the proposed structure is in 111 
keeping with the neighborhood character. This is a very large-scale building on a 1/3-acre lot. It 112 
will be a  prominent and dominant structure  and will have somewhat of a commercial 113 
appearance. He agreed that the applicant’s property is currently maintained very well. This does 114 
not change the fact that a garage of the proposed scope will have a commercial appearance . 115 
Granting the variance could open the door in the future to similar requests which would erode 116 
the character of the neighborhood over time. A couple of cars in a garage is a typical residential 117 
use, but 6+ cars it becomes a bit of a commercial application. While the present owners maintain 118 
the property well, there is no telling what future owners would do with the proposed structure. 119 
A future owner may want to repair cars  or open a business . This proposal introduces the 120 
opportunity to diminish the appearance of the neighborhood, and it is  not consistent with the 121 
residential use of nearby properties. It is specifically called out in the declaration of covenants 122 
and restrictions that the residential nature of the neighborhood  should be maintained. There is 123 
a potential for incremental losses in value of neighboring properties. The purpose of a variance 124 
is to eliminate a hardship, but this seems to be more of an issue of convenience.  125

property line as anything could be. The proposed garage is larger than her house. The proposed 129

height of the garage cannot be camouflaged with a fence. From her backyard, she will be looking 130
